title: Leibniz's monadology of observing entities

tellings.quote: Now this is something that Livinets suggested back in 1700. He had this monodology

plain: The idea that reality is built out of observing entities is an old one, according to the researcher Don Hoffman, who tells Michels that the philosopher Leibniz suggested it "back in 1700" in his monadology, a picture of the world as made of simple, perceiving units. Hoffman offers it in passing and without naming a source, to show that his own view, that conscious observers come first and the physical world follows from them, has deep roots.
